rule: Hit feedback is a per-entity queue of short-lived damage numbers, each carrying an owner hue, a 1.5 s life, a one-pixel rise every 25 ms and a cap of ten per entity. Death is a timer started by the server's death packet that gates one overlay and plays a fixed death track. Music is keyed to state: a login loop, a random war track on entering war mode, a fixed death track. The client has no tutorial code; the first-30-minute content (tips, intro, first fight, loot, hub) is server-sent and not in the donor.
keep: Per-target damage-number queue with a hard cap so multi-attacker fights stay readable
Owner-coloured damage numbers (own hue vs other hue)
Short death beat: one overlay, one music cue, timer-bounded
Preselected default in the creation flow so the first confirm is one tap
Server-authored tip windows: text from the server, client only shows it and requests next or previous
change: No profession tree or six-facet city map: first screen is the ring
Replace the random war track with a fixed, placed stinger on the first fight
Make the death beat a single line plus the next state (town hall), not an idle overlay
look_test: On a 375-wide phone, play one 60-second ring clip twice. A: current hit feedback. B: own hits in one hue, attacker hits in another, numbers rising for 1.5 s, capped at ten per target, three attackers on screen. Dom judges whether his own numbers read at a glance and whether the death beat feels like a beat or a pause.
